title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for heart failure.

HPI: Patient is an 89-year-old female with a history of chronic systolic heart failure. She reports being stable over the last month with no significant increase in shortness of breath or peripheral edema. She denies any recent hospitalizations or significant weight fluctuations. Patient reports she has been adherent to her diuretic regimen.

Vitals: BP 128/74, HR 76, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 98.2 F, Weight 158 lbs.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or fatigue.
Respiratory: Negative for cough or dyspnea.
Cardiovascular: Negative for palpitations or chest pain.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea or abdominal pain.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Carvedilol 6.25mg twice daily
- Furosemide 40mg daily

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. S1, S2 heard. No murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: No pitting edema noted.

Assessment:
1. Chronic systolic heart failure: Patient is currently stable. Symptoms were reviewed and she denies increased congestion.

Plan:
1. Chronic systolic heart failure: Continue current medication regimen. Will monitor weight and symptoms. Follow up in 3 months.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
May 14, 2026
explanations: The provider addressed chronic systolic heart failure at this visit, so it is supported: I50.22.

distractors.why: Status plus a plan in the assessment supports the diagnosis.
